Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Troubleshooting Common Challenges and Staying on Track.
Even when you’ve got a personalized plan and the best intentions, life has a way of throwing you curveballs. Maybe you’re traveling, feeling under the weather, or dealing with a family emergency—or you just hit a stretch where motivation’s low. Any of these can throw your routine off track, right? So, how do you keep going when things don’t go as planned?
Here’s the first principle to remember: expect imperfection. Life’s always moving, and no routine is immune to interruption. Instead of seeing those disruptions as failures, try thinking of them as just part of the journey—a natural ebb and flow. The real secret is gentle persistence. When you’re thrown off, give yourself permission to come back to your routine as soon as you can, and do it without beating yourself up.
When things get tough, it’s helpful to have what I like to call a “minimum viable routine.” That’s just a scaled-back version of your morning practice—something you can do in just a few minutes. Maybe it’s a single minute of quiet, a quick affirmation, or scribbling down just one intention for the day. The goal here? Keep that thread of consistency alive, even when time or energy feels scarce.
So, how can you troubleshoot the most common challenges? Here are a few practical strategies:
Pack a little “travel kit” with the essentials for your routine—things like a small journal, headphones for guided meditation, or maybe your favorite book. Make technology your friend: set reminders, use habit-tracking apps, or listen to audio versions of your practices when you’re on the move.
And if you miss a day? Look at it as a learning opportunity—not proof that you’ve failed.
Another challenge that pops up is boredom—or just feeling stuck. When routines become too familiar, they can lose their spark. If you notice this happening, shake things up a bit. Try a new form of exercise, experiment with different meditation styles, or swap out your reading material. And if you want a little extra accountability—or just some company—invite a friend or family member to join you. It can make things feel fresh and fun again.
Let me share a couple of real-life examples. Someone who travels a lot might use hotel gyms for exercise and listen to affirmations on their commute. A parent with a newborn might shift their routine to nap times, focusing on just one or two key practices. These little adaptations keep the spirit of the routine alive, no matter what’s changing around you.
When it comes down to it, your most powerful tool is self-compassion. Progress isn’t always a straight line, and setbacks are totally normal. By treating yourself with patience and a little kindness, you’ll find it’s much easier to weather challenges and come back to your routine—often with even more commitment than before.
